name: Lottielab
one_liner: Browser-based, collaborative motion design editor for creating, editing and shipping Lottie animations to web and apps.
what_it_offers: A Figma-like web editor (design and animate modes, keyframe timeline, presets) that imports Figma, SVG, Lottie and After Effects assets. It exports Lottie, dotLottie, GIF, MP4, WebM and Telegram stickers. It also offers interactive Lotties, Lottie hosting/CDN (Livelink) with embed links, a file-size optimizer, a free template library (icons, illustrations, logos, mockups, showreels, social media), and free web converters (Lottie to GIF/MP4/WebM, SVG to Lottie). Its AI Magic Animator Figma plugin generates four editable animation variations from a Figma frame. The same company also runs Burp, a separate AI video and motion editor.
tech_stack: Next.js (pages router; marketing site and app share one build). Browser export uses an ffmpeg worker (libx264 MP4, VP9 WebM with alpha). Outputs are Lottie JSON/dotLottie, played with @lottielab/lottie-player (TypeScript, lottie-web based, web component + React component).
portfolio_fit_reason: Useful for a signature animated logo, hero micro-animation or animated case-study UI demo, but Lottie is optional polish for most portfolios, and watermark-free Lottie export needs the paid Pro plan.
client_ok_note: Terms let creators keep IP and don't ban commercial use of their own exports; Pro ($18/editor/mo) removes watermarks. Template licensing is undefined, so use your own artwork.
best_use_for_portfolio: Turn Figma frames of a logo mark or a key project screen into a short animated logo reveal or a looping case-study UI demo. Export it as Lottie on Pro and embed it with the MIT @lottielab/lottie-player React component in the hero or project header.
tier_reason: Good for an animated logo or case-study UI demo, but Lottie is optional polish for most portfolios, and watermark-free export needs Pro.
pick_over_overlaps: Use it for simple linear icon or illustration loops imported from Figma or After Effects, or when the team already ships Lottie.
score_rationale: One of the easiest ways to make lightweight, vector, interactive motion (logo reveals, hero micro-animations, icon states) that drops into a React/Next.js site through an MIT player, and Magic Animator speeds up Figma-to-motion. Held back by watermarked free exports, paywalled Lottie export, no agent/MCP authoring path, a stale player library and unclear template licensing.
free_tier: Free (hobbyists and students): unlimited files, Lottie and SVG upload, Figma import, and GIF and MP4 export. Free exports are watermarked. The pricing page's meta description says 'Upgrade to remove watermarks'. The editor's upgrade prompt lists 'Export without a watermark' first, and export code checks a per-user shouldWatermark flag. The downgrade screen warns that Free users get 'No new watermark-free exports for Lottie, Video, or GIF' and that Livelink-hosted animations will be watermarked. Lottie export, HD/4K video, Telegram stickers, team library and hosting/CDN are Pro features.
paid_entry_label: Pro $18/editor/mo billed monthly ($12/editor/mo billed annually); unlimited viewer collaborators, watermark-free exports
commercial_use_license: The Terms are still dated April 23, 2024 (re-checked live 2026-09-14; no newer version or separate template license page exists). Users keep IP ownership of content they submit but grant Lottielab a non-exclusive, royalty-free, transferable, sub-licensable worldwide licence over it. There is no explicit ban on commercial use of your own exports, but free exports are watermarked, so production use effectively needs Pro. Templates have no specific license. The templates page calls them 'free, easy to edit motion design templates' without stating rights. The Terms' only general grant covers website materials for 'personal, non-commercial transitory use', which may be read to cover templates, so commercial template use is unconfirmed. The @lottielab/lottie-player npm package is MIT.
agent_friendly: The npm package @lottielab/lottie-player (MIT, web component + React) had 49,384 downloads between Aug 13 and Sep 11, 2026, so an agent can embed exported Lottie JSON or CDN URLs. docs.lottielab.com/llms.txt exists but covers only editor and export docs. No official Lottielab MCP server, CLI or public authoring API was found; npm search shows only the player. Competitor LottieFiles has official MCP servers.
maintenance_signal: Active in 2026, mostly on its AI products. The Magic Animator Figma plugin shipped Version 18 on June 13, 2026 and Version 19 on July 17, 2026, has 73.3k users, and has comments from the past week. The pricing page is live with © 2026. Burp, Lottielab's AI video/motion editor announced September 2025, is now live at burp.com with paid tiers. The core pieces are older: the main 'Lottielab - Figma to Lottie' plugin was last updated Nov 13, 2024, the GitHub lottielab/lottie-player repo (36 stars) last got a push and release v1.1.3 on 2024-12-23, and the old /whats-new changelog pages now return 404. Magic Animator beta 2.0 was announced Oct 8, 2025. The site claims 500,000+ designers.
caveats: Free plan exports are watermarked and can't export Lottie (only GIF/MP4), so the web-native, watermark-free output needs Pro. Pricing is per editor. Lottie playback adds JS weight compared with CSS/Motion animations. There is no MCP or API, so AI agents can't author animations. lottie-player was last released Dec 2024 and the main Figma plugin was last updated Nov 2024. Magic Animator runs on credits (referral codes give 10 free credits), and its paid credit pricing is not published on magicanimator.com or lottielab.com. Template licensing is undefined, and the Terms haven't changed since April 2024. Burp is a separate product with its own pricing.
unverified_fields: Magic Animator paid credit pricing (only the 10 free referral credits are confirmed)
Commercial license for free templates (no template license exists; the Terms' materials clause is non-commercial)
What the watermark looks like on a real free export (confirmed from pricing metadata, upgrade and downgrade copy, and export code; not tested, since that needs an account)
Burp pricing amounts (tier names and credits are visible; prices did not render)
